title: Glossary Q&A — The Lost Supply (Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit)
content:
**Entry.** For a lost, stolen or damaged medication replacement under the Retail Pharmacy Network Benefit, the lost supply depends on where the member's medication came from: when the member has a home delivery shipment of the drug and it is dated later than the most recent paid retail claim for the drug or that retail claim carries a reversal, the most recent shipment is the lost supply; when, with no such shipment, the most recent paid retail claim carries a reversal, nothing was dispensed and the lost supply counts zero days; otherwise it is the most recent paid retail claim.

## Questions on the entry

**Where is a home delivery shipment read from?** From the member's Home Delivery Pharmacy shipped orders for the drug. The most recent shipment is the one with the latest shipment date, and it brings its shipment date, days supply and quantity.

**A retail claim dated April 4 and a Home Delivery Pharmacy shipment dated April 18 (hypothetical). Which is the lost supply?** The shipment of April 18, because it is dated later.

**A shipment dated April 4 and a retail claim dated April 18?** The retail claim of April 18, provided it carries no reversal.

**The April 18 retail claim carries a reversal and there is a shipment dated April 4?** The shipment of April 4: a reversed retail claim gives way to a shipment whatever their dates.

**The April 18 retail claim carries a reversal and there is no shipment?** Nothing was dispensed; the lost supply counts zero days.

**A shipment and no paid retail claim at all?** The shipment is the lost supply.

**What does the lost supply bring with it?** Its date (date of service or shipment date), its days supply and its quantity.
